response.reason: This lens audits contract completeness, owner/root default-entry semantics, transition-group guard collisions, and containment. Key finding: HumanDriving is a top-level state (not owned by AutonomousMode), root has a valid unconditional-trigger initial edge [*]->HumanDriving (line 19/tr_0001 satisfies NL3-INIT-1), and containment/declaration contracts are satisfied by exact state inventory. However, AutonomousMode's own initial pseudostate edge ([*]->AutoInitial) is conditional/triggered (event Enter_Autonomous_Mode) with no unconditional fallback, matching W_INITIAL_UNCONDITIONAL_MISSING diagnostics for the Autonomous composite and the refuted initial-entry verify check at transition:line:12. This is a distinct owner-entry defect not covered by any supplied contract; I derive one additional_contracts row for it. Guard_disjointness for auto final's outgoing alternatives (AutoInitial->[*] and AutoFinal->[*] both trigger on the same compound event with no distinguishing guard) is examined per NL4.2-DERIVED-a846a312efcd228fa321. Endpoint/guard/trigger contracts for NL4/NL4.2/NL5 are compared against the exact FCSTM transitions: line 20 (HumanDriving->Autonomous) has trigger front_distance_10 but guard=null though NL4 requires a separate guard field; NL4.2's event and guard are both folded into one compound opaque trigger name with guard=null on both AutoInitial->[*] and AutoFinal->[*] edges, so trigger_set and guard obligations cannot be confirmed as separately realized; NL5's endpoint HumanDriving->[*] exists, but Autonomous (also named in the contract's locus as part of 'current operating scope') has no exit edge to Final/[*], so that scope reading is an exact absence in the complete transition inventory.

(2) NL4.2-CONTAIN/ENDPOINT/EVENT/GUARD contracts are satisfied via AutoInitial->[*] and AutoFinal->[*] (lines 14,15) plus Autonomous->HumanDriving (line 18) macro chain gated on R45RouteToken==5; the guard 'brake pressed' from NL4.2-GUARD-1 is not present anywhere in the closed transitions (only a single combined event name), which is a wrong_guard defect. issues.strongest_rebuttal: Because pyfcstm resolves the trigger per exact source state (AutoInitial vs AutoFinal), the two transitions are already structurally distinguished by their distinct source states even without an explicit guard, so no guard collision exists at the model level.
issues.title: AutoInitial->[*] and AutoFinal->[*] alternatives are operationally indistinguishable under the identical compound condition

issues.basis: exact_source_inventory.transitions (no row with source=Autonomous and target=@final or [*]); inspection_equivalent_facts.states Autonomous outgoing_transition_refs=[transition:line:18] only (to HumanDriving, not Final); fcstm_model.text has no 'Autonomous -> [*]' line.
issues.expected: On PowerOff, the current operating scope (which the contract's locus_names indicate may be either HumanDrivingMode or AutonomousMode) must transition to a Final state.
issues.observed: The exact closed-model and source inventories show a Power_Off-triggered edge only from HumanDriving to [*] (line 21 / tr_0006); AutonomousMode has no outgoing Power_Off edge to any final state, so if the autonomous operating scope is active when power is turned off, there is no authored transition realizing NL5's termination obligation from that scope.
issues.reason: NL5-ENDPOINT-1's locus_names explicitly list both HumanDrivingMode and AutonomousMode as candidate operating scopes reaching Final; the complete transition inventory contains no Autonomous-to-Final (or Autonomous-to-[*]) edge, so this exact source/target pair is absent from the closed model and must be recorded as a candidate absence rather than silently satisfied by the HumanDriving-only edge.
issues.requirement_quote: when power off, it will transit to final state
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The NL and PlantUML source only ever place the Power Off edge on HumanDriving (line 13 of the .puml), so 'the current operating scope' may be read narrowly as always meaning HumanDrivingMode specifically (since the system always returns to HumanDriving before power-off matters), making the single authored edge sufficient and this candidate a mis-scoped reading.
issues.title: Only HumanDriving has an authored Power-Off exit to Final; AutonomousMode as an 'operating scope' has no such exit

issues.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts.transitions[transition:line:19].reachable_from_initial=false and triggers=[Power_On]; inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL line:19; verify_facts.non_proved initial-entry:transition:line:19 status=refuted has_trigger=true; verify_facts.non_proved event-consumer:Power_On reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]; NL-CONTRACT-NL3-INIT-1 binding_hints owner=root/system, target=HumanDrivingMode, event=power on.
issues.expected: The root/system scope's initial pseudostate edge to HumanDrivingMode on PowerOn must be an unconditional, operationally reachable default entry establishing HumanDrivingMode as the system's first operating state.
issues.observed: The closed FCSTM's root-owned edge [*] -> HumanDriving (transition:line:19) carries trigger Power_On (has_trigger=true) rather than being an unconditional default initial edge; verify_facts explicitly refutes this initial-entry check (check_id=initial-entry:transition:line:19, status=refuted, details.has_trigger=true). Consistently, inspection_equivalent_facts marks this transition reachable_from_initial=false and the Power_On event's reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[] (declared consumer is transition:line:19 only), meaning the very edge that must realize this initial-entry obligation is not reachable from the machine's own entry semantics -- the deterministic diagnostic INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL further confirms the pseudostate edge carries a trigger it should not have as an unconditional default.
issues.reason: The contract requires a genuine top-level entry into HumanDrivingMode upon PowerOn as the root/system's initial operating state. The closed FCSTM shows the sole edge carrying this event is structurally present but deterministically refuted as an initial-entry fact and structurally unreachable-from-initial according to inspection_equivalent_facts, which is a precise behavioral defect on this exact contract rather than a satisfied endpoint.
issues.requirement_quote: when power on, the system turn into human driving mode
issues.strongest_rebuttal: One could argue the edge exists at the correct source (@initial:__root__ / [*]) and target (HumanDriving) per the exact_source_inventory (tr_0001), so the endpoint pair itself is present; a reviewer could claim S2 endpoint existence discharges this NL obligation. However the contract's normative language ('on PowerOn, the system must enter...as its initial operating state') requires this be the actual default/triggered initial entry, and the closed-model's own verify_facts and reachability explicitly refute that the transition realizing it is reachable from initial, so endpoint presence alone does not rebut the refuted initial-entry status.
issues.title: Root-owned PowerOn initial entry to HumanDriving is conditional and operationally unreachable as a top-level default entry

issues.basis: fcstm_model transitions at line 14/15 (guard=null, trigger=human_steering_cmd_brake_pressed_in_AutoFinal) and line 18 (guard=R45RouteToken==5); exact_source_inventory transition tr_0005 event field combines human_steering_cmd||brake_pressed||in(AutoFinal) with no separate guard field; NL-CONTRACT-NL4.2-GUARD-1 requires distinct guard=brake pressed.
issues.expected: The transition returning from AutoFinal to HumanDrivingMode must independently carry the data guard 'brake pressed' distinct from the human-steering-cmd event/trigger.
issues.observed: In the closed FCSTM, AutoFinal -> [*] (transition:line:15) carries only the single opaque combined trigger 'human_steering_cmd_brake_pressed_in_AutoFinal' with guard=null and effects=[R45RouteToken=5]; the subsequent macro-joined Autonomous -> HumanDriving (transition:line:18) carries guard 'R45RouteToken == 5', an internal route-control condition, not the semantic 'brake pressed' data guard required by NL. No transition in the complete inventory carries a guard field evaluating brake-pressed state.
issues.reason: NL4.2 explicitly separates the trigger event ('receive human steering cmd') from the guard condition ('brake pressed'), requiring them as two independently evaluated properties. The closed FCSTM collapses both into one undifferentiated event name and uses an unrelated internal route-token guard on the macro-joined transition, so the specific brake-pressed guard obligation is not present as its own transition property.
issues.requirement_quote: transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final)
issues.strongest_rebuttal: One could argue the combined event name 'human_steering_cmd || brake_pressed || in (AutoFinal)' textually encodes the brake-pressed condition as part of one opaque trigger, so the semantic content is preserved even though it is not represented as a separate guard field; under this reading the requirement is satisfied by trigger inclusion rather than a distinct guard expression.
issues.title: The auto final -> HumanDrivingMode return path carries no independent 'brake pressed' guard, only a combined opaque event name
